title: Changing languages: reducts, expansions, and completeness
summary: Translate first-order symbols, preserve truth and proofs, and remove the countability restriction from deductive completeness.
abstract: Adding a name or renaming a relation changes the language in which we speak about a structure. We make precise when an old sentence keeps its meaning after this change, and how an old proof becomes a proof in the larger language. Each formula uses only finitely many symbols, even when the whole language is uncountable. Combining this observation with compactness lets us apply the countable-language completeness theorem to a finite vocabulary, then translate the resulting proof back. Thus every first-order consequence has a finite proof for any set of function and relation symbols.
